subject.title: Agent declared tools != effective session tools: no strict inheritance mode, no visibility, no clipping reason trace

question: What strict/effective tool contract should OpenClaw expose for session tools: visibility-only diagnostics, an opt-in fail-closed strict mode, or the current effective-only reporting model?
rationale: The requested behavior changes operator-visible security semantics, adds config/API surface, and may fail existing sessions closed when runtime layers intentionally clip tools.

options.title: Visibility-first diagnostics
options.body: Expose declared, effective, removed, and blocked-reason metadata without making strict parity the default failure mode.

options.title: Opt-in strict mode
options.body: Add an explicit strict config option that fails sessions when effective tools diverge, with docs, tests, and doctor/upgrade guidance.

options.title: Keep effective-only reporting
options.body: Treat current `tools.effective` plus audit logs as sufficient and decline strict parity as too much config/security surface.

recommendation.title: Visibility-first diagnostics
recommendation.body: Expose declared, effective, removed, and blocked-reason metadata without making strict parity the default failure mode.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work spans the effective-tool Gateway path, capability profile refactor, and the security-sensitive policy surface.
